land.text: the Beyşehir lakeland, a frontier carved out of the declining Seljuk Sultanate of Rum

predecessors.note: Infobox: preceded by the Sultanate of Rum. The page describes the Eshrefids as a frontier state set up by Oghuz Turkish clans after the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum declined; no handover date is given.

land.text: Beyşehir and the Eshrefid lands, taken by the Ilkhanid viceroy Timurtash in October 1326

successors.note: The Timurtash page has the Ilkhanid viceroy capture Beyşehir and drown the last bey in the lake on 9 October 1326. The Eshrefids infobox lists the Chobanids as successor (Timurtash was a Chobanid, Chupan's son, but the Eshrefids page does not explain the link). Who held the land after Timurtash's flight in December 1327 is not on any page opened.

capitals.name: Beyşehir
capitals.note: Infobox lists Beyşehir as the only capital, without years; the Timurtash page has the 1326 siege end at Beyşehir.

rulers.name: Mubariz al-Din Mehmed Bey
rulers.note: The Eshrefids page says the dynasty 'ended when Mubariz al-Din Mehmed was executed by Timurtash' but dates his reign 1302-1320; the Timurtash page names the bey executed in 1326 as Suleiman II.

rulers.name: Suleiman II Bey
rulers.note: Drowned in Lake Beyşehir by Timurtash, 9 October 1326 (Timurtash page).

correction.text: the 1305 shape projected back to the founding: Beyşehir and the lakeland, the only land the pages name

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1305 but the infobox says 'Established: 1280' (the Anatolian beyliks table says 1285). The pages give no territory before 1305, so the 1305 shape stands in; treat 1280-1304 as approximate.

13,289 km2 around Beyşehir; the page gives no area or boundary, so there is no infobox figure to compare. The shape also reaches the western edge of Konya's plain; the Karamanids page dates 'Conquest of Konya: 1308' but does not say who held Konya's west before. Unverified beyond the capital.

correction.text: unchanged shape; it holds to 9 October 1326, not 1325

keyframe_review.note: The 13,239 km2 shape differs from 1305's by 50 km2 (grid noise); no page explains a change in 1314. Cliopatria ends the row in 1325 but the Timurtash page has Beyşehir taken and Suleiman II drowned on 9 October 1326, so the shape is extended by one year (years only).

region.text: Beyşehir and the lakeland round it

ledger.note: 1280: Suleiman I ibn Eshref founds the Eshrefid principality at Beyşehir. Infobox 'Established: 1280'; the page describes a frontier state set up by Oghuz Turkish clans after the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum declined. The Anatolian beyliks table gives 1285; the page gives the capital, not a boundary, so the region is Cliopatria's 1305 shape.

1326: the Ilkhanid viceroy Timurtash takes Beyşehir and ends the Eshrefids. The page has him 'executing their bey Süleyman II by drowning him in Lake Beyşehir on 9 October 1326' after capturing Beyşehir; the extent of the land taken is the Eshrefid shape (the page names only the city).

1326: the Eshrefids end. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1326'; month from the Timurtash page (9 October). Infobox lists the Chobanids as successor; the land passed to the Ilkhanid viceroy Timurtash (a son of Chupan), who held Anatolia until he fled in December 1327.

wars.name: Timurtash's conquest of the Eshrefids
wars.outcome: Ilkhanid victory: Timurtash captured Beyşehir and had the last bey, Suleiman II, drowned in the lake on 9 October 1326.
wars.note: The page gives no start of the campaign, so no contest_start is coded; the zone is the Eshrefid shape itself and went from owner to conqueror in one step.

certainty.note: A small frontier principality in the Lakes region of Anatolia; no page gives a boundary, so the whole life is drawn soft.

sources.title: Eshrefids
sources.note: Founding (1280), end (1326), capital Beyşehir, the three beys; a thin page: no territory, no area.

sources.title: Timurtash
sources.note: The 1326 capture of Beyşehir and the drowning of Suleiman II on 9 October 1326.

sources.title: Karamanids
sources.note: Checked for the Eshrefids and Beyşehir: only 'Conquest of Konya: 1308' and an undated Karamanid capture of Beyşehir; nothing used.

sources.note: Table row: Eshrefid, founder Suleyman ibn Eshref Bey, Beyşehir, 1285-1326.

notes: Pages: Eshrefids (thin), Timurtash (the 1326 end), Karamanids and Anatolian beyliks (checked). The Cliopatria row ends in 1325, one year before the dated end (9 October 1326). The infobox successor 'Chobanids' is the family of the Ilkhanid viceroy Timurtash (son of Chupan); it is not Cliopatria's Chobanids row (1344-1362, Tabriz). The page contradicts itself on who was executed (Mubariz al-Din Mehmed in the lead, Suleiman II on the Timurtash page and in the ruler table). Who held Beyşehir after 1327 (Karamanids, Eretna) is not on any page opened. Cliopatria's shape reaches Konya's plain; a gap-filler may check it against the Karamanids' 1308 capture of Konya.
